"Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly." This upbeat assessment, together with a 25 bp hike to 2–2¼ percent and guidance for “further gradual” increases, aligns with Taylor-style prescriptions when the output gap is positive and with forward-looking New Keynesian rules (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) that emphasize anchoring inflation expectations and interest-rate smoothing. The implementation choice to set IOER at 2.20% and the ON RRP at 2.00% is consistent with the post-2008 ample-reserves “floor” framework discussed by Goodfriend (2002), providing reliable control of the funds rate. With risks described as “roughly balanced” and inflation near a symmetric 2% target, the tone is positive with a measured hawkish tilt rather than aggressively restrictive.
